title: What ABA files are and why PayTrade uses them
content:
What ABA files are and why PayTrade uses them

A short conceptual guide to the Australian Bankers' Association (ABA) payment file format and how PayTrade uses it to save you time when paying multiple suppliers, sub-contractors or trust beneficiaries at once.

What is an ABA file?

An ABA file (sometimes called a direct entry file, bulk payment file, or cemtex file) is a small, fixed-width text file with a .aba extension. It contains:

  • A header line identifying your business and your bank's APCA / Direct Entry User ID.
  • One transaction line per payment, with the recipient's BSB, account number, name, amount, and a short reference.
  • A footer line with the total amount and the number of transactions.

You upload the single file to your bank's internet banking portal, authorise it once, and the bank disburses every payment in the batch.

Which Australian banks accept ABA files?

ABA is the standard Australian bulk-payment format. It is supported by every major bank and most credit unions, including:

  • Commonwealth Bank (CBA / NetBank Business)
  • Westpac (Corporate Online / WIB)
  • NAB (NAB Connect)
  • ANZ (Internet Banking for Business / Transactive)
  • Bendigo Bank, Macquarie, Suncorp, ING, BOQ, St George, Bank of Melbourne, BankSA
  • Most credit unions and customer-owned banks

The exact menu name in your bank's portal differs ("Upload payment file", "Direct Entry", "Batch payments") but the file format is the same.

Why PayTrade generates ABA files for you

On a typical project there can be dozens of sub-contractor payments, retention releases and supplier bills due in the same week. Without ABA you would type each one into your bank's portal — copying BSBs and account numbers across, double-checking amounts, and authorising every transaction individually. That is slow and error-prone.

With PayTrade:

  1. You select the payments you want to make on the Payments To Do page.
  2. PayTrade generates a properly formatted .aba file using the recipient details already stored against each contract.
  3. You upload that file to your bank once. The bank pays everyone.
  4. Optionally, PayTrade marks the corresponding payments as paid and triggers payment notices automatically.

Which subscription plans include ABA generation?

ABA generation is included on the Standard, Advanced and Pro Audit plans. It is not available on the Basic (Free) plan.

If you are on the Basic plan, the Generate ABA button is greyed-out on Payments To Do and the backend will return the message "ABA files cannot be generated. Please upgrade your subscription plan." if generation is attempted.

Next steps

  • Read Setting up your bank account for ABA generation to add your APCA / Direct Entry User ID and verify the account is ABA-ready.
  • Then read Generating and using an ABA file (day-to-day workflow) for the step-by-step payment routine.

title: Setting up your bank account for ABA generation
content:
Setting up your bank account for ABA generation

Step-by-step instructions to make a sender bank account ABA-ready in PayTrade — including how to obtain your APCA (Direct Entry) User ID from your bank, which fields are mandatory, BSB formatting rules, and how to confirm the account is ready before you try to generate a file.

Before you start

Make sure you are on the Standard, Advanced or Pro Audit subscription plan. ABA generation is not available on the Basic (Free) plan — see What ABA files are and why PayTrade uses them.

Step 1 — Get your APCA / Direct Entry User ID from your bank

An APCA number (also called a Direct Entry User ID) is a unique 6-digit identifier your bank issues when they enable bulk-payment file uploads on your account. It is not your customer number, your BSB, or your internet-banking login.

To obtain it:

  1. Log in to your business banking portal (NetBank Business, NAB Connect, Westpac Corporate Online, ANZ Transactive, etc.).
  2. Look for a menu called Direct Entry, Batch payments, File uploads, or ABA upload.
  3. If you do not see this menu, contact your bank's business banking line and ask: "Please enable Direct Entry / ABA file uploads on my account and provide my APCA User ID."
  4. Your bank may charge a small monthly fee and may take 1–3 business days to enable it.

Tip: If your bank issues a 4- or 5-digit number, just enter it as-is. PayTrade will pad it correctly when writing the file.

Step 2 — Add or open your bank account in PayTrade

  1. From the sidebar, click Bank Accounts.
  2. Click Add Bank Account at /user/bank-accounts/add, or click Edit on an existing account.
  3. Fill in the mandatory fields:
    • Account Name — the name on the account, exactly as your bank holds it.
    • Account Type — Cash Account, Project Trust Account (PTA), or Retention Trust Account (RTA).
    • BSB Number — 6 digits, no spaces or dashes (e.g. 062000). PayTrade formats it as 062-000 in the file.
    • Account Number — your bank account number.
    • Financial Institution — pick from the list (CBA, WBC, NAB, ANZ etc.). PayTrade uses this to write the 3-letter institution code in the ABA header.
  4. Save the account.

Step 3 — Add your APCA number (edit screen only)

The APCA Number field is only visible on the Edit Bank Account screen — not on Add. This is intentional, because most users get their APCA ID from the bank a few days after opening the account.

  1. Open the bank account you just created and click Edit.
  2. Scroll to the APCA Number field.
  3. Enter the number your bank gave you (digits only).
  4. Click Save.

Important: Without an APCA number, PayTrade will silently skip this account when generating ABA files — no file will be produced for payments going out of it.

Step 4 — Make sure recipient details are complete

For every sub-contractor or supplier you intend to pay via ABA, the contract must have:

  • Recipient BSB (6 digits)
  • Recipient account number
  • Recipient account name

Any sub-payment missing the recipient BSB or account number is silently skipped from the ABA file. You can review and complete recipient bank details on each contract's Bank Details tab.

Step 5 — Verify the account is ABA-ready

Quick check before your first run:

  • The account shows an APCA number on the Bank Accounts list / detail screen.
  • Your subscription plan is Standard, Advanced or Pro Audit.
  • At least one sub-payment in Payments To Do is drawn from this account and has full recipient bank details.

If all three are true, the Generate ABA button will be active and the file will produce successfully.

Common reasons ABA generation fails

SymptomMost likely causeFix
Warning: "ABA files cannot be generated. Please upgrade your subscription plan."You are on the Basic (Free) plan.Upgrade to Standard, Advanced or Pro Audit.
Generate ABA button is greyed-outSubscription does not include ABA, or no eligible payments are selected.Check plan; tick at least one sub-payment.
No file is produced for one of your sender accountsThat sender account has no APCA number.Edit the bank account, add the APCA number, save.
A payment you expected is missing from the fileRecipient BSB or account number is blank on that contract.Open the contract, complete the bank details, regenerate.
Bank rejects the file with "invalid User ID"APCA number is wrong or not yet activated by the bank.Confirm the APCA ID with your bank's business banking line.

Next steps

Once your sender account is ABA-ready, read Generating and using an ABA file (day-to-day workflow) to learn the day-to-day routine.

title: Generating and using an ABA file (day-to-day workflow)
content:
Generating and using an ABA file (day-to-day workflow)

A step-by-step walkthrough of the routine you will follow each time you batch-pay sub-contractors, suppliers or retention releases through your bank using a PayTrade-generated ABA file.

Before you start

  • Your subscription is Standard, Advanced or Pro Audit.
  • The sender bank account has an APCA number saved (see Setting up your bank account for ABA generation).
  • Recipient BSB, account number and account name are complete on every contract you intend to pay.

Step 1 — Open Payments To Do

  1. From the sidebar, click Payments To Do.
  2. You will see all sub-payments that are due — full payments, part payments, retention releases, withdrawals, bank charges, and any pay-less amounts.

Step 2 — Select the payments to include

  1. Tick the checkbox next to each sub-payment you want to pay in this batch.
  2. You can mix payments from different sender accounts in one selection — PayTrade will produce one ABA file per sender account automatically.
  3. You can mix Cash, Project Trust, and Retention Trust accounts.

Step 3 — Click Generate ABA

Click the Generate ABA button at the top of the table. PayTrade will validate the selection and prompt you with the question:

"Do you want to mark these payments as paid?"

Step 4 — Choose Yes or No (this only affects status, not the file)

The ABA file is generated either way. Your answer only controls what happens to the payment statuses inside PayTrade after the file is created.

Your choiceWhat happens
Yes — mark as paidFile downloads. Each payment is marked paid confirmed (retention releases marked retention confirmed). Payment notices are automatically triggered for the affected sub-payments.
No — do not mark as paidFile downloads. No payment statuses change. No notices are sent. You will need to mark each payment as paid manually later.

Recommended: Choose Yes only after you have actually uploaded and authorised the file in your bank, so PayTrade's records match what your bank has done.

Step 5 — Download the .aba file(s)

PayTrade saves each generated file to Payments To Do → ABA history tab and offers an immediate download link. Filenames follow the pattern <sender-account>-<sender-name>-<timestamp>.aba so you can tell them apart when you have generated more than one in a session.

Step 6 — Upload the file to your bank

  1. Log in to your business banking portal.
  2. Open the Direct Entry, Batch payments, or Upload payment file menu.
  3. Upload the .aba file from PayTrade.
  4. Review the totals — the bank should display the same total amount and transaction count that PayTrade showed you.
  5. Authorise the batch using your bank's normal approval process (token, SMS, second-signatory etc.).

Tip: If you generated separate files for different sender accounts, upload each one to its matching account in your bank.

Step 7 — What happens to payment statuses and notices

  • If you chose Yes — mark as paid, the affected payments now show as Paid in Payment History, and the payment notices have been queued for delivery to recipients.
  • If you chose No, the payments still appear under Payments To Do with their original status. Open each payment and click Mark as Paid after the bank confirms the disbursement.
  • You can re-download any past ABA file from Payments To Do → ABA history for audit purposes — the file, the sender account, and whether it was marked paid are all retained.

FAQ

Does just generating the ABA file mark payments as paid?
No. Generating the file alone does not change any statuses. Only choosing Yes at the "mark as paid" prompt updates statuses and triggers notices.

Can I undo a "Mark as paid"?
Yes — open the affected payment in Payment History and edit it back to its previous state. The ABA file itself is unaffected.

Why did one of my payments not appear in the file?
The most common cause is missing recipient BSB or account number on the contract. PayTrade silently skips lines without those fields. See the troubleshooting block in Setting up your bank account for ABA generation.

Why did no file get produced for one of my sender accounts?
That sender account has no APCA number. Open it in Bank Accounts, click Edit, add the APCA, save, then re-generate.

Why is the Generate ABA button greyed-out?
Either your subscription plan does not include ABA generation (Basic / Free) or no eligible sub-payments are selected. See What ABA files are and why PayTrade uses them for the plan list.
